data.narrative:
The Lumber Manufactory is a Series C robotics and manufacturing company founded by Michael Grasso and Andrew Arsht, having raised $53.1M to date. Valuation analysis relies on a peer universe of nine private robotics firms and one public comparable (277810.KQ), spanning Series B through Series D stages. Key private peers include Exotec ($2.0B, Series D), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), and Hadrian ($1.6B, Series D).

Two methods anchor the valuation. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement to the $53M capital proxy, yielding $90M. Peer-median triangulation across seven same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables produces a $1.6B implied value, with the peer set ranging from $1.0B to $2.0B. The wide dispersion reflects heterogeneity in stage and maturity within the robotics sector.

The triangulated valuation range spans $77M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $870M. The substantial gap between stage-progression and peer methods reflects the bootstrap nature of the former against market-wide capital deployment patterns. Key uncertainties include relative technology differentiation versus the peer set, revenue trajectory visibility, and sector-wide funding environment shifts. The median estimate of $870M serves as a working point pending materialization of revenue or market-specific milestones.
